key_insight: Ideal liquid crystal elastomers couple mesogen orientation with network deformation, enabling reversible actuation and soft deformation through continuously connected stress-free states.
engineering_relevance: The theory provides a constitutive foundation for modeling LCE actuators and compliant structures with programmable shape changes and low-stress deformation.
method: Connect anisotropic Gaussian-chain statistics to neo-classical continuum elasticity.
Explain spontaneous deformation and stripe-domain soft elasticity through non-quasi-convex free energy.
Use quasi-convex relaxation to classify three macroscopic response phases in polydomain LCEs.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a theoretical review and phase classification, without reporting experimental datasets or quantitative validation.
watch_item: Ideal soft elasticity assumes no crosslinking-state memory; practical simulations may require network nonideality, director-gradient elasticity, and rate-dependent effects.
paper_title: Elastic theory of ideal liquid crystal elastomers
